response: Emergency general surgery laparotomies are indeed an area of concern and need for improvement, particularly when it comes to 30-day and 1-year mortality rates. The mortality rate is especially high in patients over the age of 70. To improve outcomes, several strategies can be considered, including increasing acute surgical care manpower, early recognition of patients requiring emergency surgery, development of clear management protocols, and centralization of emergency surgical services to specialist centers with multidisciplinary teams. Additionally, involving care of the elderly physicians in hospital and related community outreach services for post-discharge care may also be beneficial. Overall, a multifaceted approach is necessary to address the high mortality rates associated with emergency general surgery laparotomies.
